name: godot-mcp-tool

tools.name: godot_status
tools.description: Check the connection to Godot: which project is used, whether the Godot editor with the "Godot MCP Tool" plugin is connected, and which Godot executable and version are available. Call it first when another Godot tool reports a connection problem.

tools.name: editor_launch
tools.description: Start the Godot editor for the project and wait until its "Godot MCP Tool" plugin connects, so the editor tools work. Use it when godot_status says the editor is not running. The editor keeps running after this session; it does nothing when the editor is already connected.

headless.description: Start the editor without a window, as on a server; screenshots need a window. Default: with a window, or without one when the server runs with GODOT_MCP_HEADLESS=1.

tools.name: project_create
tools.description: Create a new Godot 4 project for a game from scratch: project.godot with the name, the renderer, Jolt Physics, the window size and warnings for GDScript declarations without a static type, a main scene with a camera and a light, .gitignore, and the godot MCP addon installed with its plugin enabled. A server that started without a project works on the new one right away; start its editor with editor_launch.

path.description: The folder of the project, relative to the folder Claude Code runs in or absolute, such as "capsule-walk". It is created when missing and must be empty apart from hidden files and notes (.md). Default: the folder Claude Code runs in.

name.description: The name of the game. Default: the folder name in words, such as "Capsule Walk".

renderer.description: forward_plus (default) for desktop 3D, mobile for phones and lighter 3D, gl_compatibility for the web and old hardware.

window_size.description: The window size [width, height] in pixels. Default: [1152, 648].

tools.name: project_info
tools.description: Summarize the Godot project: name, main scene, renderer, 3D physics engine, window size, autoloads, enabled plugins, global classes (class_name), the indentation style of .gd files and the top-level folders. Call it once when starting work on a project.

tools.name: project_settings_get
tools.description: Read project settings (project.godot) by full name or by prefix. Pass names, prefix or both. Unknown names come back with similar existing names.

prefix.description: Read every setting whose name starts with this, such as "display/window/".

tools.name: project_settings_set
tools.description: Change project settings and save project.godot, for example the main scene (application/run/main_scene) or the window size. Each value is read back; the result lists what applied and the previous values, so the change can be reverted.

values.description: Setting names mapped to new values, such as {"application/run/main_scene": "res://levels/arena.tscn"}. Values use the same formats as node properties.

tools.name: user_data_get
tools.description: Read user://, the folder where the game keeps saved games, settings and logs: without a path, every file with its size and the time it changed; with a file, its text. Use it to check what the game saved after game_run. Works without the editor. To clear saves, delete them with user_data_delete when unsafe tools are on.

path.description: A file or folder in the user data, such as "user://save.json" or "saves"; the user:// prefix may be left out. Default: the whole folder, listed.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes of a file to show.

tools.name: editor_rescan
tools.description: Make the editor pick up files changed outside it, such as scripts, scenes or assets written to disk and GDExtension libraries rebuilt by a native build: reload the rebuilt GDExtensions, rescan the project, import new assets and reload changed scripts, as the editor does when its window gets focus. Call it after writing files or rebuilding a GDExtension, before using them in scenes or validating scripts that use them.

tools.name: editor_screenshot
tools.description: Render the 3D scene open in the editor from the editor camera or from given views, without the grid and gizmos; the editor camera stays where it is. Check placement and scale from more than one side, such as ["front", "top", "iso"]. With animation, render the poses of an animation at several times, such as the steps of a walk cycle. A UI or 2D scene, such as a HUD or a menu, renders as the game window would show it, at the window size of the project or at given sizes, such as 16:9 and 4:3 side by side. The lighting of 3D scenes is the editor preview, so check the final look with game_screenshot. Needs the editor with a window.

views.description: Render the 3D scene from these angles instead of the editor camera, up to 6 in one labelled image: a preset "front" (from +Z), "back", "left" (from -X), "right", "top" or "iso", framed on the whole scene; {"preset": "front", "target": "Player"} to frame one node; or {"position": [0, 8, 12], "look_at": [0, 0, 0]} for a camera at a point. Each view also takes "fov", "label" and "render", such as {"preset": "iso", "render": "unshaded"}.

target.description: A node to frame instead of the whole scene, such as "Player".

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees. Default: 50.

label.description: Caption of the view in the image.

render.description: Draw this view as a debug view of the 3D viewport instead of with materials and light: "unshaded" shows colors without light, to tell a dark room from a black material; "lighting" shows only the light; "overdraw" shows where transparent surfaces pile up; "wireframe" shows the triangles (editor_screenshot only); "normals" shows the surface normals (Forward+ only).

position.description: Camera position [x, y, z] in world coordinates.

look_at.description: The point the camera looks at. Default: the center of target, or of the whole scene.

target.description: A node to frame instead of the whole scene, such as "Player".

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees. Default: 50.

label.description: Caption of the view in the image.

render.description: Draw this view as a debug view of the 3D viewport instead of with materials and light: "unshaded" shows colors without light, to tell a dark room from a black material; "lighting" shows only the light; "overdraw" shows where transparent surfaces pile up; "wireframe" shows the triangles (editor_screenshot only); "normals" shows the surface normals (Forward+ only).

animation.description: Render the poses of an animation at given times without running the game, one labelled image per time in one picture, from the editor camera or from one given view. Method calls and sounds of the animation stay silent, and the animated values are put back afterwards.

player.description: Path of the AnimationPlayer relative to the scene root, such as "Hero/AnimationPlayer".

name.description: The animation to pose, such as "walk".

times.description: Seconds from the start of the animation to pose the scene at. Default: four times spread over the animation, such as 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 of a looping one.

sizes.description: For a UI or 2D scene, the window sizes to render it at, such as [[1920, 1080], [1440, 1080]] for 16:9 and 4:3 in one labelled image; the layout follows the stretch mode and aspect of the project. Default: the window size of the project.

max_size.description: The longest side of the image in pixels. Default: 1280.

format.description: png (default), or jpeg for a smaller file.

compare_to.description: Compare the new picture with an earlier one, by the path that an earlier screenshot gave (the last 100 are kept) or as an image of the project, such as "res://screenshots/level.png": the result says how much changed and where, and outlines the changes in the picture. Take both with the same views and size. Time, particles and temporal anti-aliasing make two runs differ; run the game with fixed_fps and take both at the same physics frame to compare runs.

tolerance.description: With compare_to, how much a color channel may change, from 0 to 1, before its pixel counts as changed. Default: 0.1.

tools.name: input_map_get
tools.description: List the input actions of the project (Project Settings → Input Map) with their keys, mouse buttons and joypad events. The built-in ui_ actions are left out unless include_builtin is true.

actions.description: Actions to show, such as ["move_forward", "jump"]. Default: every action of the project.

include_builtin.description: Also list the built-in ui_ actions, such as ui_accept.

tools.name: input_map_set
tools.description: Create, change or remove input actions of the project and save project.godot. Give each action its full list of events; scripts then read it with Input.is_action_pressed("move_forward"). A game that is already running keeps its old actions until it starts again.

actions.description: Action names mapped to their full list of events, such as {"move_forward": ["W", "Up"], "jump": ["Space", {"type": "joypad_button", "button": "a"}]}. Events: key names such as "W", "Space", "Up" or "Ctrl+S"; {"type": "mouse_button", "button": "left"}; {"type": "joypad_button", "button": "a"}; {"type": "joypad_motion", "axis": "left_y", "direction": -1}. Use {"events": [...], "deadzone": 0.3} to set the deadzone, and null to remove an action.

tools.name: audio_buses_get
tools.description: Read the audio bus layout of the project, as the Audio panel of the editor shows it: each bus in order with its volume in dB, the bus it sends to, mute, solo, bypass and its effects, and the file the layout is saved in. Players such as AudioStreamPlayer pick a bus by name with their "bus" property. Works without the editor. With in_game, listen to the running game: the level of each bus and the players that play, to tell a muted bus, a silent volume or a player that never starts from a sound that plays.

in_game.description: Listen to the running game instead: the loudest peak of each bus over a few physics frames, whether that is silence, and the players that are playing, with their bus and stream. Works with or without the editor.

window_physics_frames.description: With in_game, how long to listen, in physics frames (60 per second by default). Default: 30.

tools.name: audio_buses_set
tools.description: Add, change and remove buses of the audio bus layout of the project, as the Audio panel of the editor does, and save the layout file at once, so that the game starts with them: such as a Music and an Effects bus, each with its own volume, both sending to Master. Then pick the bus of each player with node_set_properties, such as {"bus": "Music"}; a player whose bus does not exist plays on Master.

buses.description: Buses to add or change, in order; settings that are left out keep their value. Example: [{"name": "Music", "volume_db": -6}, {"name": "Effects"}].

name.description: The bus to add or change, such as "Music". A new bus is added after the others.

volume_db.description: The volume in decibels: 0 leaves the sound as it is, -6 is about half as loud, -80 silent.

send.description: The bus that this one sends its sound to, which must come before it in the layout. Default for a new bus: "Master".

solo.description: Silence every bus that is not solo.

bypass_effects.description: Let the sound through without the effects of the bus.

remove.description: Buses to remove by name. Master stays.

tools.name: scene_create
tools.description: Create a new scene file with a root node, save it and open it in the editor, so the scene and node tools work on it next. A 3D level usually has a "Node3D" root; pass a res://….tscn path as root_type to inherit from another scene.

path.description: Where to save the new scene, such as "res://levels/arena.tscn". The file must not exist yet; missing folders are created.

root_type.description: Type of the root node: an engine class such as "Node3D", a class_name from the project, or a res://….tscn path to create a scene inherited from it.

root_name.description: Name of the root node. Default: the file name in PascalCase, so "arena.tscn" gets "Arena".

tools.name: scene_open
tools.description: Open a scene in the editor and make it the current scene, which the scene and node tools use when no scene is given. Tools that change a scene open it themselves, so this is mainly for choosing the default scene or showing a scene to the user.

path.description: The scene to open, such as "res://levels/arena.tscn", or "main" for the main scene of the project.

tools.name: scene_save
tools.description: Save scenes from the editor to disk: the current scene, a given scene, or all open scenes. Changes made with the scene and node tools stay unsaved until then, as in the editor. Save when a logical change is complete. Refuses with a conflict when a script changed on disk while the editor has unsaved changes to it.

scene.description: The scene to save, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

all.description: Save every open scene instead of one.

tools.name: scene_get_tree
tools.description: Show the node tree of a scene as compact text: node names and types, attached scripts, instanced scenes and groups. Use it before changing a scene to learn the node paths that the node tools take. Reads the scene open in the editor by default, or any scene by its res:// path. The nodes inside an instanced scene are listed when its Editable Children is on, or for every instance with expand_instances.

scene.description: The scene to read, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; a scene that is not open is read from disk. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

max_depth.description: How many levels below the root to show.

max_nodes.description: The most nodes to list; hidden children are counted.

expand_instances.description: Also include the nodes inside instanced scenes, such as "Enemy2/Mesh", which node_set_properties changes for that instance only. Default: only the instances themselves, and the nodes of instances whose Editable Children is on.

tools.name: scene_batch_edit
tools.description: Apply many scene changes in one call and as one Undo step: add, delete, change, move and duplicate nodes, set their groups, connect and disconnect signals. Later operations can use the nodes that earlier ones added or renamed. If any operation fails or any property is rejected, nothing is changed and the error names the operation; a value that the engine adjusts, such as a size raised to the minimum of a control, is kept and reported. Use it to build or rework a scene.

type.description: What to add: an engine class such as "MeshInstance3D", a class_name from the project, or a scene to instance such as "res://props/crate.tscn".

name.description: Name of the new node. Default: the type name; a taken name gets a number.

parent.description: Path of the parent node relative to the scene root. Default: "." (the root).

index.description: Position among the children of the parent. Default: after the last child.

properties.description: Property names mapped to values, in the formats of node_set_properties, such as {"position": [0, 1, 0], "mesh": {"new": "BoxMesh"}}.

paths.description: Paths of the nodes to delete, relative to the scene root, such as ["Enemies/Goblin"]. Children go with their parent.

path.description: Path of the node relative to the scene root, such as "Player/Camera"; "." is the root itself.

add.description: Groups to add the node to, such as ["enemies", "damageable"].

remove.description: Groups to take the node out of.

parent.description: Path of the new parent, such as "Props"; "." is the scene root. Default: the current parent.

name.description: A new name for the node.

index.description: The new position among the children of the parent; 0 is the first.

keep_global_transform.description: Keep a 3D node where it is in the world when its parent changes. Default: true.

shape.description: trimesh follows every triangle and suits static level geometry; convex and simplified_convex wrap the mesh in one convex hull; multiple_convex splits it into up to 32 hulls for concave moving objects; box, capsule, cylinder and sphere fit a primitive to the mesh.

placement.description: static_body (default) adds a StaticBody3D child with the shapes, so that bodies cannot pass through the mesh; sibling adds CollisionShape3D nodes next to the mesh, for a mesh that is already part of a physics body.

axis.description: The axis of a capsule or a cylinder fitted to a mesh that is not one. Default: the longest side of the mesh.

from.description: Path of the node that emits the signal, such as "Button" or "Door/Area".

to.description: Path of the node whose method is called. Default: "." (the scene root).

method.description: The method to call, such as "_on_button_pressed".

binds.description: Extra values passed to the method after the signal arguments, such as ["door_a"].

deferred.description: Call the method at the end of the frame instead of at once.

from.description: Path of the node that emits the signal, such as "Button" or "Door/Area".

to.description: Path of the node whose method is called. Default: "." (the scene root).

method.description: The method to call, such as "_on_button_pressed".

operations.description: The changes in order. Each is {"op": a tool name, ...the parameters of that tool except scene}, such as {"op": "node_add", "type": "CharacterBody3D", "name": "Player"}, {"op": "node_set_properties", "path": "Player", "properties": {"position": [0, 1, 0]}} or {"op": "signal_connect", "from": "Start", "signal": "pressed", "method": "_on_start_pressed"}. op is node_add, node_delete, node_set_properties, node_set_groups, node_reparent, node_duplicate, node_save_as_scene, node_make_local, node_add_collision, signal_connect or signal_disconnect.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: node_add
tools.description: Add a node to a scene: an engine class, a class_name from the project, or an instance of another scene, with its properties set at once. One Undo step in the editor; the scene stays unsaved until scene_save. The result reports which properties applied.

type.description: What to add: an engine class such as "MeshInstance3D", a class_name from the project, or a scene to instance such as "res://props/crate.tscn".

name.description: Name of the new node. Default: the type name; a taken name gets a number.

parent.description: Path of the parent node relative to the scene root. Default: "." (the root).

index.description: Position among the children of the parent. Default: after the last child.

properties.description: Property names mapped to values, such as {"position": [0, 1, 0], "mesh": {"new": "BoxMesh", "size": [2, 1, 2]}}. Formats: numbers, booleans and text as JSON; vectors as [x, y, z] or "Vector3(0, 1, 0)"; rotation is in radians, rotation_degrees takes degrees; colors as "#ff8800", "orange" or [r, g, b, a] with channels from 0 to 1; enums by option name ("Double-Sided") or number; flags as a list of names; physics, render and navigation layers as a list of layer numbers or of the names the project gives them (["world", "enemies", 5]); resources as a "res://…" path, or {"new": "Class", …properties} to create one; the items of a Theme as "Button/styles/normal" or "Label/font_sizes/font_size", the points of a curve as "point_count", "point_0/position" and the handles "point_0/in" and "point_0/out", the items of a MeshLibrary as "item/0/name" and "item/0/mesh"; a script as "res://….gd"; node references and node paths, such as node_a of a joint, as paths relative to the node ("../Player") or to the scene root ("Player"); Transform3D, Basis, AABB and Rect2 in Godot syntax ("Transform3D(…)"). Scripting properties such as global_position work too. A path changes one part only: "mesh:size" a property of the node's own mesh, "position:y" one coordinate. Every value is read back after it is set.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: node_delete
tools.description: Delete nodes and their children from a scene as one Undo step. If any path is not found, nothing is deleted. The scene root and nodes inside instanced scenes cannot be deleted here.

paths.description: Paths of the nodes to delete, relative to the scene root, such as ["Enemies/Goblin"]. Children go with their parent.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: node_duplicate
tools.description: Duplicate a node with its children, groups, scripts and signal connections, as one Undo step. The copy goes right after the original, or under parent; properties are set on the copy, such as {"position": [4, 0, 0]}.

path.description: Path of the node relative to the scene root, such as "Player/Camera"; "." is the root itself.

name.description: Name of the copy. Default: the name of the original with a number, such as "Crate2".

parent.description: Put the copy under this node instead of right after the original.

properties.description: Property names mapped to values, such as {"position": [0, 1, 0], "mesh": {"new": "BoxMesh", "size": [2, 1, 2]}}. Formats: numbers, booleans and text as JSON; vectors as [x, y, z] or "Vector3(0, 1, 0)"; rotation is in radians, rotation_degrees takes degrees; colors as "#ff8800", "orange" or [r, g, b, a] with channels from 0 to 1; enums by option name ("Double-Sided") or number; flags as a list of names; physics, render and navigation layers as a list of layer numbers or of the names the project gives them (["world", "enemies", 5]); resources as a "res://…" path, or {"new": "Class", …properties} to create one; the items of a Theme as "Button/styles/normal" or "Label/font_sizes/font_size", the points of a curve as "point_count", "point_0/position" and the handles "point_0/in" and "point_0/out", the items of a MeshLibrary as "item/0/name" and "item/0/mesh"; a script as "res://….gd"; node references and node paths, such as node_a of a joint, as paths relative to the node ("../Player") or to the scene root ("Player"); Transform3D, Basis, AABB and Rect2 in Godot syntax ("Transform3D(…)"). Scripting properties such as global_position work too. A path changes one part only: "mesh:size" a property of the node's own mesh, "position:y" one coordinate. Every value is read back after it is set.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: node_reparent
tools.description: Move a node to another parent, rename it, or change its place among its siblings, as one Undo step; its children move with it. 3D nodes keep their place in the world unless keep_global_transform is false. Node paths that pointed at the moved nodes, such as a RemoteTransform3D remote_path or an exported NodePath, are updated.

path.description: Path of the node relative to the scene root, such as "Player/Camera"; "." is the root itself.

parent.description: Path of the new parent, such as "Props"; "." is the scene root. Default: the current parent.

name.description: A new name for the node.

index.description: The new position among the children of the parent; 0 is the first.

keep_global_transform.description: Keep a 3D node where it is in the world when its parent changes. Default: true.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: node_save_as_scene
tools.description: Save a node and its children as a scene file of their own and put an instance of that scene in their place, as Save Branch as Scene in the editor does: one Undo step, and the instance stays where the node was. Use it to turn something built in a level, such as an enemy, into a scene that other levels can instance with node_add. The new file is written at once; the changed scene stays unsaved until scene_save.

path.description: Path of the node relative to the scene root, such as "Player/Camera"; "." is the root itself.

file.description: The new scene file, such as "res://enemies/enemy.tscn". It must not exist yet; missing folders are created.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: node_make_local
tools.description: Turn an instance of another scene into nodes of this scene, as Make Local in the editor does, as one Undo step: its nodes stop following changes to the instanced scene file and can then be moved, deleted and changed here like any other node. To change one instance but keep it linked to its scene, set properties of its nodes with node_set_properties instead.

path.description: Path of the node relative to the scene root, such as "Player/Camera"; "." is the root itself.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: node_find
tools.description: Find nodes in a scene by name, type, group or attached script; every given criterion must match. Returns their paths for the other node tools. The nodes inside an instanced scene are searched when its Editable Children is on, or in every instance with expand_instances.

name.description: Part of the node name, or a pattern with * and ?, such as "Enemy*". Case does not matter.

type.description: A node class or class_name. Subclasses match too, so "Light3D" finds every light.

group.description: A group the node belongs to, such as "enemies".

script.description: The attached script, as a res:// path or a file name such as "player.gd".

scene.description: The scene to read, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; a scene that is not open is read from disk. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

expand_instances.description: Also include the nodes inside instanced scenes, such as "Enemy2/Mesh", which node_set_properties changes for that instance only. Default: only the instances themselves, and the nodes of instances whose Editable Children is on.

tools.name: node_get_properties
tools.description: Read the properties of a node, or of several nodes at once: those that differ from their defaults, or the ones named. Each value comes with its type, in Godot syntax; enums list their options, masks their layers. Use it to check nodes before or after changing them.

path.description: Path of the node relative to the scene root, such as "Player/Camera"; "." is the root itself.

paths.description: Read several nodes at once instead of path, such as ["Player", "Enemies/Goblin"]: each comes back in its own block, and a node that is not found is reported among the others.

names.description: Properties to read, such as ["position", "mesh"], or paths into a resource or a value, such as "mesh:size" or "position:y". Default: every property whose value differs from its default.

include_defaults.description: Without names, also list properties at their default values. The list gets long.

scene.description: The scene to read, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; a scene that is not open is read from disk. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: node_get_bounds
tools.description: Measure the box that a 3D node and its children take up in world coordinates: center, size and corners, from its meshes and CSG shapes, or from its collision shapes when it has none. For a Control or a 2D node, measure its rectangle in canvas pixels, from controls, sprites, polygons, lines and tile maps, or from 2D collision shapes; a control also says whether it fits the window of the project. Measures one node, or several at once. Use it to check placement and scale, such as whether a crate rests on the floor, a door is wide enough for the player or a health bar stays on screen.

path.description: Path of the node relative to the scene root, such as "Level/Crate"; "." measures the whole scene. With in_game, a path in the running game, such as "Player".

paths.description: Measure several nodes at once instead of path, such as ["Crate", "Ramp", "Player"]; each comes back in its own block.

scene.description: The scene to read, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; a scene that is not open is read from disk. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

in_game.description: Measure the nodes in the running game instead, where they may have moved. Needs a game started from the editor.

tools.name: scene_raycast
tools.description: Cast a ray through a 3D scene and return the first thing it hits: the position, the surface normal, the distance and the node, whether a collision shape or a visible mesh without collision. Straight down by default, to find the ground under a point; between two points to check a line of sight, such as whether an enemy sees the player. With in_game, cast in the running game.

from.description: Where the ray starts, [x, y, z] in world coordinates, such as [0, 10, 0].

to.description: Where the ray ends. Default: 1000 m straight down from "from", to find the ground under a point.

exclude.description: Nodes the ray passes through, with their children, such as the node being placed.

in_game.description: Cast in the running game instead, against its current state. Needs a game started with game_run.

scene.description: The scene to cast in, as a res:// path; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: node_snap_to_floor
tools.description: Move 3D nodes straight down or up until each touches what is below it, a collision shape or a visible mesh, as one Undo step. A node stops where the first point of its collision shapes, or of its meshes when it has none, meets the surface, so nothing sinks into the ground and a node tilted like a slope lies flat on it. With align, each node is first turned so that its up axis follows the surface under it. Use it to put props on uneven ground, on slopes or on top of other objects.

paths.description: The 3D nodes to place, such as ["Crate", "Props/Barrel"].

align.description: First turn each node so that its up axis follows the surface under it, such as a crate on a slope, then place it. Default: false, which keeps the rotation.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main"; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: node_add_collision
tools.description: Give a MeshInstance3D a collision built from its mesh, as Mesh → Create Collision Shape in the editor does, as one Undo step, so that players and other bodies cannot pass through it. The result compares the size of the collision with the size of the mesh. CSG nodes take use_collision instead, and imported models their import settings.

path.description: Path of the node relative to the scene root, such as "Player/Camera"; "." is the root itself.

shape.description: trimesh follows every triangle and suits static level geometry; convex and simplified_convex wrap the mesh in one convex hull; multiple_convex splits it into up to 32 hulls for concave moving objects; box, capsule, cylinder and sphere fit a primitive to the mesh.

placement.description: static_body (default) adds a StaticBody3D child with the shapes, so that bodies cannot pass through the mesh; sibling adds CollisionShape3D nodes next to the mesh, for a mesh that is already part of a physics body.

axis.description: The axis of a capsule or a cylinder fitted to a mesh that is not one. Default: the longest side of the mesh.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: node_set_properties
tools.description: Set several properties of a node as one Undo step, including script (a res://….gd path) and resources (a res:// path, or {"new": "Class", …} to create one). Every value is read back: the result lists what applied, what was rejected and why, and what the engine changed, for example by clamping. A node inside an instanced scene, such as "Enemy2/Mesh", changes for that instance only: Editable Children of the instance is turned on, as in the editor, so that the change is saved with this scene.

path.description: Path of the node relative to the scene root, such as "Player/Camera"; "." is the root itself.

properties.description: Property names mapped to values, such as {"position": [0, 1, 0], "mesh": {"new": "BoxMesh", "size": [2, 1, 2]}}. Formats: numbers, booleans and text as JSON; vectors as [x, y, z] or "Vector3(0, 1, 0)"; rotation is in radians, rotation_degrees takes degrees; colors as "#ff8800", "orange" or [r, g, b, a] with channels from 0 to 1; enums by option name ("Double-Sided") or number; flags as a list of names; physics, render and navigation layers as a list of layer numbers or of the names the project gives them (["world", "enemies", 5]); resources as a "res://…" path, or {"new": "Class", …properties} to create one; the items of a Theme as "Button/styles/normal" or "Label/font_sizes/font_size", the points of a curve as "point_count", "point_0/position" and the handles "point_0/in" and "point_0/out", the items of a MeshLibrary as "item/0/name" and "item/0/mesh"; a script as "res://….gd"; node references and node paths, such as node_a of a joint, as paths relative to the node ("../Player") or to the scene root ("Player"); Transform3D, Basis, AABB and Rect2 in Godot syntax ("Transform3D(…)"). Scripting properties such as global_position work too. A path changes one part only: "mesh:size" a property of the node's own mesh, "position:y" one coordinate. Every value is read back after it is set.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: gridmap_get_cells
tools.description: Read the cells of a GridMap: the blocks of its mesh library by name and number, how many cells use each, the box the cells fill and the cells themselves with their block and orientation, ordered by y, then z, then x. Use it to check a level built of blocks, whole or one box at a time. Works without the editor when "scene" is given.

path.description: Path of the GridMap node relative to the scene root, such as "Level/Ground".

from.description: One corner of the box of cells to read, [x, y, z] in cells, such as [-4, 0, -4]. Give "to" with it. Default: every cell.

to.description: The opposite corner of the box, included, such as [3, 0, 3].

max_cells.description: The most cells to list; the counts cover every cell.

scene.description: The scene to read, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; a scene that is not open is read from disk. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: gridmap_set_cells
tools.description: Put blocks of the mesh library of a GridMap on its cells, or erase them, as one Undo step: whole boxes of cells, such as a floor or a wall, and single cells, with blocks named as in the library. Cells are whole numbers on the grid, not meters: cell [x, y, z] sits at [x, y, z] times cell_size. Read the blocks and cells with gridmap_get_cells first.

path.description: Path of the GridMap node relative to the scene root, such as "Level/Ground".

boxes.description: Boxes of cells to fill with one block each, in order, so that a later box paints over an earlier one: a floor from [-4, 0, -4] to [3, 0, 3] is 64 cells; a ring of walls is a box of walls with a floor box inside it.

from.description: One corner, [x, y, z] in cells.

item.description: The block: its name in the mesh library, such as "Wall", or its number; null erases the cells.

orientation.description: How the block is turned, as an orthogonal index from 0 to 23. Turned around y: 0 for 0°, 16 for 90°, 10 for 180°, 22 for 270°. Default: 0, as in the mesh library.

cells.description: Single cells to set after the boxes.

position.description: The cell, [x, y, z] in cells.

item.description: The block: its name in the mesh library, such as "Wall", or its number; null erases the cells.

orientation.description: How the block is turned, as an orthogonal index from 0 to 23. Turned around y: 0 for 0°, 16 for 90°, 10 for 180°, 22 for 270°. Default: 0, as in the mesh library.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: meshlibrary_create
tools.description: Build the MeshLibrary of a GridMap from a scene of blocks, as the editor's Scene → Export As → MeshLibrary does: each MeshInstance3D with a mesh becomes an item named after the node, with its mesh and materials, the collision shapes of its StaticBody3D children and the navigation mesh of a NavigationRegion3D child. update: true changes an existing library and keeps the ids of its items, which the cells of a GridMap store. Then set mesh_library of the GridMap to the file and paint it with gridmap_set_cells. Save the scene of the blocks first; needs the editor.

scene.description: The saved scene of the blocks, such as "res://blocks/blocks.tscn": every MeshInstance3D in it with a mesh becomes a block named after the node, with the collision shapes of its StaticBody3D children and the navigation mesh of a NavigationRegion3D child.

path.description: The MeshLibrary file to write, such as "res://blocks/blocks.tres".

update.description: Update the library at path: blocks keep their ids by name, new blocks get new ids, and blocks the scene no longer has stay. Needed when the file exists, since the cells of a GridMap store the ids.

apply_transforms.description: Keep the transform that each block has in the scene, such as a rotation, in its item. Default: false, as the Import from Scene of the editor does, so blocks laid out side by side in the scene each sit in the middle of their cell.

tools.name: tilemap_get_cells
tools.description: Read the cells of a TileMapLayer: its TileSet with the tile size, the physics layers and each source with its texture, tiles and how many of them collide; how many cells use each tile, the rectangle the cells fill and the cells themselves, ordered by y, then x. Use it to check a 2D level of tiles, whole or one rectangle at a time. Works without the editor when "scene" is given.

path.description: Path of the TileMapLayer node relative to the scene root, such as "Level/Ground".

from.description: One corner of the rectangle of cells to read, [x, y] in cells, such as [0, 0]. Give "to" with it. Default: every cell.

to.description: The opposite corner of the rectangle, included, such as [29, 15].

max_cells.description: The most cells to list; the counts cover every cell.

scene.description: The scene to read, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; a scene that is not open is read from disk. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: tilemap_set_cells
tools.description: Paint tiles of the TileSet of a TileMapLayer on its cells, or erase them, as one Undo step: whole rectangles, such as the ground or a wall, and single cells, each tile given by its [column, row] in the atlas of its source. Cells are whole numbers on the grid, not pixels: cell [x, y] sits at [x, y] times the tile size, and y grows downward. Read the tiles and the cells with tilemap_get_cells first.

path.description: Path of the TileMapLayer node relative to the scene root, such as "Level/Ground".

rects.description: Rectangles of cells to fill with one tile each, in order, so that a later one paints over an earlier one: ground 30 tiles wide is {"from": [0, 10], "to": [29, 10], "atlas": [0, 0]}.

atlas.description: The tile as [column, row] in the atlas of its source, such as [0, 0] for the first one; null erases the cells.

source.description: The source of the tile in the TileSet. Default: the only source, when the TileSet has one.

alternative.description: An alternative of the tile, such as a flipped copy. Default: 0, the tile itself.

cells.description: Single cells to set after the rectangles.

atlas.description: The tile as [column, row] in the atlas of its source, such as [0, 0] for the first one; null erases the cells.

source.description: The source of the tile in the TileSet. Default: the only source, when the TileSet has one.

alternative.description: An alternative of the tile, such as a flipped copy. Default: 0, the tile itself.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: signal_list
tools.description: List the signal connections saved in a scene, or every signal of one node with its arguments and connections. Use it before signal_connect to learn the signal names and the parameters a method needs.

path.description: A node whose signals to list with their arguments and connections, such as "Door/Area". Default: every saved connection of the scene.

scene.description: The scene to read, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; a scene that is not open is read from disk. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: signal_connect
tools.description: Connect a signal of a node to a method of a node in the scene, saved with the scene like a connection made in the editor, as one Undo step. The method must already exist with matching parameters; if it does not, the error names the function to add to the script.

from.description: Path of the node that emits the signal, such as "Button" or "Door/Area".

to.description: Path of the node whose method is called. Default: "." (the scene root).

method.description: The method to call, such as "_on_button_pressed".

binds.description: Extra values passed to the method after the signal arguments, such as ["door_a"].

deferred.description: Call the method at the end of the frame instead of at once.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: signal_disconnect
tools.description: Remove a saved signal connection from a scene, as one Undo step.

from.description: Path of the node that emits the signal, such as "Button" or "Door/Area".

to.description: Path of the node whose method is called. Default: "." (the scene root).

method.description: The method to call, such as "_on_button_pressed".

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: resource_create
tools.description: Create a resource file (.tres) with its properties set at once and save it: a material, physics material, environment, curve, or a resource of a class of the project. Use it for resources that several nodes or scenes share and assign it to them by its res:// path; a resource that only one node uses can be created right in the node property with {"new": "Class", …} instead. The result reports which properties applied.

path.description: Where to save the new resource, as a res:// path ending in .tres, such as "res://materials/ice.tres". Missing folders are created; an existing file is never replaced.

type.description: The resource class: an engine class such as "StandardMaterial3D", "PhysicsMaterial", "Environment" or "Curve", or a class_name of the project that extends Resource.

properties.description: Property names mapped to values, such as {"position": [0, 1, 0], "mesh": {"new": "BoxMesh", "size": [2, 1, 2]}}. Formats: numbers, booleans and text as JSON; vectors as [x, y, z] or "Vector3(0, 1, 0)"; rotation is in radians, rotation_degrees takes degrees; colors as "#ff8800", "orange" or [r, g, b, a] with channels from 0 to 1; enums by option name ("Double-Sided") or number; flags as a list of names; physics, render and navigation layers as a list of layer numbers or of the names the project gives them (["world", "enemies", 5]); resources as a "res://…" path, or {"new": "Class", …properties} to create one; the items of a Theme as "Button/styles/normal" or "Label/font_sizes/font_size", the points of a curve as "point_count", "point_0/position" and the handles "point_0/in" and "point_0/out", the items of a MeshLibrary as "item/0/name" and "item/0/mesh"; a script as "res://….gd"; node references and node paths, such as node_a of a joint, as paths relative to the node ("../Player") or to the scene root ("Player"); Transform3D, Basis, AABB and Rect2 in Godot syntax ("Transform3D(…)"). Scripting properties such as global_position work too. A path changes one part only: "mesh:size" a property of the node's own mesh, "position:y" one coordinate. Every value is read back after it is set.

tools.name: resource_get
tools.description: Read a resource file such as a material, physics material or environment, or an imported one such as a texture: its type, the properties that differ from their defaults or the ones named, each with its type in Godot syntax, and the files it depends on; for a texture also its size in pixels. Scenes are read with scene_get_tree instead.

path.description: The resource file, as a res:// path such as "res://materials/ice.tres".

names.description: Properties to read, such as ["albedo_color", "roughness"], paths such as "next_pass:albedo_color", or methods without arguments whose names start with is_, get_, has_ or can_, such as "get_length()". Default: every property whose value differs from its default.

include_defaults.description: Without names, also list properties at their default values. The list gets long.

tools.name: resource_set_properties
tools.description: Set several properties of a resource file such as a material or physics material as one Undo step and save the file, so the scenes that use it, the game and the tests see the change at once. Every value is read back: the result lists what applied, what was rejected and why, and what the engine changed. Imported files such as textures and models are changed through their import settings instead, with asset_import_settings_set.

path.description: The resource file, as a res:// path such as "res://materials/ice.tres".

properties.description: Property names mapped to values, such as {"position": [0, 1, 0], "mesh": {"new": "BoxMesh", "size": [2, 1, 2]}}. Formats: numbers, booleans and text as JSON; vectors as [x, y, z] or "Vector3(0, 1, 0)"; rotation is in radians, rotation_degrees takes degrees; colors as "#ff8800", "orange" or [r, g, b, a] with channels from 0 to 1; enums by option name ("Double-Sided") or number; flags as a list of names; physics, render and navigation layers as a list of layer numbers or of the names the project gives them (["world", "enemies", 5]); resources as a "res://…" path, or {"new": "Class", …properties} to create one; the items of a Theme as "Button/styles/normal" or "Label/font_sizes/font_size", the points of a curve as "point_count", "point_0/position" and the handles "point_0/in" and "point_0/out", the items of a MeshLibrary as "item/0/name" and "item/0/mesh"; a script as "res://….gd"; node references and node paths, such as node_a of a joint, as paths relative to the node ("../Player") or to the scene root ("Player"); Transform3D, Basis, AABB and Rect2 in Godot syntax ("Transform3D(…)"). Scripting properties such as global_position work too. A path changes one part only: "mesh:size" a property of the node's own mesh, "position:y" one coordinate. Every value is read back after it is set.

tools.name: tileset_add_atlas
tools.description: Cut a texture into tiles and add them to a TileSet as one atlas source, creating the TileSet file when it does not exist, and save it: every tile of the given size that is not empty, each with a full square collision when asked, so that bodies stand on it. This is how a 2D level of tiles starts: then give the TileSet to a TileMapLayer and paint its cells with tilemap_set_cells.

path.description: The TileSet file to create or add to, such as "res://tiles/ground.tres".

texture.description: The image of the tiles, such as "res://tiles.png", as the editor imported it.

tile_size.description: The size of one tile in pixels, [width, height], such as [32, 32]. A new TileSet takes it as its tile_size.

collision.description: Give every tile a full square collision polygon on physics layer 0, added when the TileSet has none, so that bodies stand on the tiles. Default: false.

margins.description: Pixels to skip at the left and the top of the texture before the first tile. Default: [0, 0].

separation.description: Pixels between neighboring tiles in the texture. Default: [0, 0].

tools.name: resource_find_usages
tools.description: Find what uses a file, or the files of a folder, before moving, renaming or deleting it: the scenes and resources that refer to it, the project settings that point at it, such as the main scene or an autoload, and the lines of scripts and shaders that name its res:// path or its UID. Code is searched as text, so paths built while the game runs are not found, and code in res://addons/ is searched only for files of addons. For a folder, uses from inside the folder are left out.

path.description: A file or folder of the project, as a res:// path such as "res://materials/ice.tres" or "res://materials".

tools.name: filesystem_move
tools.description: Move or rename a file or folder of the project as the FileSystem dock does: its .import and .uid files go along, the scenes and resources that refer to it get the new path, open scenes follow, and project settings that point at it, such as the main scene or an autoload, are updated. References by UID keep working. Scripts and shaders that name the old res:// path are listed for you to change, and so are binary .scn and .res files that use it, which only the editor can rewrite. The move is not in the Undo history; move it back with filesystem_move. Refuses while a scene that it changes is open with unsaved changes.

from.description: The file or folder to move, as a res:// path such as "res://materials/ice.tres".

to.description: The new path, with the file or folder name, such as "res://surfaces/ice.tres", or "res://materials/frost.tres" to rename it. Missing folders are created; an existing file or folder is never replaced.

tools.name: asset_import_settings_get
tools.description: Read how Godot imports an asset such as a glTF, FBX or .blend model, a texture or a sound: its importer options (nodes/root_scale, nodes/root_type, materials/extract, …), the settings stored for nodes of a model, and for a model the size, nodes and collision shapes of the imported scene. Check the size first: models often arrive in centimeters, such as a character 180 units tall, and need nodes/root_scale 0.01.

path.description: The imported file, as a res:// path such as "res://models/character.glb".

tools.name: asset_import_settings_set
tools.description: Change the import settings of an asset and reimport it, so every scene that uses it gets the result. options change importer options, such as {"nodes/root_scale": 0.01} to turn centimeters into meters or {"nodes/root_type": "StaticBody3D"}; nodes give nodes of a model their own settings, such as collision with {"Body": {"generate/physics": true, "physics/shape_type": "Trimesh"}}. Primitive shapes (Box, Sphere, Cylinder, Capsule) are not fitted to the mesh: give primitive/size, primitive/radius and primitive/height in the model's own units, before root_scale, and primitive/position to move the shape from the node's origin. The result shows the size of the imported scene before and after and its collision shapes, to compare.

path.description: The imported file, as a res:// path such as "res://models/character.glb".

options.description: Importer options by name, as asset_import_settings_get lists them, such as {"nodes/root_scale": 0.01, "materials/extract": "Extract Once", "materials/extract_path": "res://materials/"}.

nodes.description: Settings for nodes of a model, keyed by node path as asset_import_settings_get lists them, such as {"Body": {"generate/physics": true, "physics/shape_type": "Capsule", "primitive/radius": 25, "primitive/height": 180}}. Settings: generate/physics, physics/body_type (StaticBody3D, RigidBody3D, Area3D), physics/shape_type (Decompose Convex, Single Convex, Trimesh, Box, Sphere, Cylinder, Capsule, Automatic), physics/layer and physics/mask (layer numbers), primitive/size, primitive/radius, primitive/height, primitive/position, primitive/rotation, generate/navmesh, generate/occluder, mesh_instance/cast_shadow, mesh_instance/layers, import/skip_import, node/node_type.

tools.name: navigation_bake
tools.description: Bake the navigation mesh of a NavigationRegion3D, or of every one in the scene, from the geometry under the region — floors and obstacles as meshes, CSG nodes or static collision shapes — as the editor's Bake NavigationMesh button does. One Undo step; the scene stays unsaved until scene_save, and the game uses the saved mesh. The result gives each region's polygon count and the area it covers, which is smaller than the floor by the agent radius; a region that gets no polygons comes with the reason, such as no geometry under it or an agent too large. Agent size and other bake settings are properties of the region's NavigationMesh: agent_radius, agent_height, agent_max_climb, agent_max_slope.

path.description: Path of the NavigationRegion3D relative to the scene root, such as "Navigation". Default: every NavigationRegion3D of the scene.

scene.description: The scene to bake in, as a res:// path; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: navigation_get_path
tools.description: Ask the navigation for the path from one point to another, as a NavigationAgent3D would get it: whether it reaches the target, its length and its points, and, when it stops short, where and how far from the target. It tells a level whose regions connect from one with a gap without running a chase. Reads the baked navigation meshes of the scene, which navigation_bake makes, or with in_game those of the running game.

from.description: Where the path starts, [x, y, z] in world coordinates, such as the position of an enemy.

to.description: Where the path should end, such as the position of the player.

navigation_layers.description: The navigation layers to walk on, by number or by the name the project gives them, as navigation_layers of a NavigationAgent3D. Default: [1], the layer of a new agent.

in_game.description: Ask the navigation of the running game instead, as its agents see it now. Needs a game started from the editor.

scene.description: The scene to ask, as a res:// path or "main"; a scene that is not open is read from disk. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: voxelgi_bake
tools.description: Bake a VoxelGI, or every one in the scene, as the editor's Bake VoxelGI button does, so that it bounces light: it voxelizes the meshes and CSG shapes with GI mode Static inside its box and saves the data next to the scene as <scene>.<VoxelGI>_data.res, or into the file the VoxelGI already uses. A VoxelGI lights nothing until it is baked, and needs a bake again after the geometry inside changes. The link to the data is one Undo step, and the scene stays unsaved until scene_save. Needs the editor with a window and the Forward+ renderer. A LightmapGI or an OccluderInstance3D has no bake method for tools; the result says which button of the editor bakes it.

path.description: Path of the VoxelGI relative to the scene root, such as "Cave/VoxelGI". Default: every VoxelGI of the scene.

scene.description: The scene to bake in, as a res:// path; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: animation_get
tools.description: Read the animations of an AnimationPlayer: each animation's length, loop mode and track count, or with name the tracks of one animation with their node paths, interpolation and keys. Track paths are relative to the player's root_node, the parent of the player by default.

player.description: Path of the AnimationPlayer relative to the scene root, such as "AnimationPlayer" or "Door/AnimationPlayer".

name.description: An animation to show with its tracks and keys. Default: list every animation of the player.

scene.description: The scene, as a res:// path; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: animation_set
tools.description: Create or replace an animation of an AnimationPlayer from tracks, as one Undo step: a value track animates one property, such as {"path": "Door:position", "keys": [{"time": 0, "value": [0, 0, 0]}, {"time": 1, "value": [0, 3, 0]}]}, with a node path relative to the parent of the player and values in the formats of node_set_properties; a method track calls methods of a node at given times, such as footsteps: {"type": "method", "path": "Walker", "keys": [{"time": 0.25, "method": "_on_footstep"}]}; an audio track plays sounds through an audio player node: {"type": "audio", "path": "Walker/Footsteps", "keys": [{"time": 0.25, "stream": "res://sounds/step.ogg"}]}. Method tracks call in the running game, not in the editor. A track the editor cannot use is rejected with the reason and the others are kept. Like the editor, it keys the current value of each newly animated property in the RESET animation, the pose that the other animations and AnimationTree blends start from; without it, a property that only some animations of a state machine animate would blend from zero. An animation plays when a script calls play("name") on the player or when the player's autoplay names it; check it in the running game with game_wait and game_get_properties.

player.description: Path of the AnimationPlayer relative to the scene root, such as "AnimationPlayer" or "Door/AnimationPlayer".

name.description: Name of the animation, such as "open"; "library/name" for an animation of another library than the default one.

length.description: Length in seconds. Default: the time of the last key.

loop.description: none (default) plays once, linear repeats, pingpong goes back and forth.

type.description: value (default) animates a property; "method" calls methods of a node; "audio" plays sounds through an audio player node.

path.description: Node and property, relative to the parent of the player: "Door:position", "Door:position:y", ".:visible" for the parent itself.

time.description: Seconds from the start of the animation.

value.description: The value, in the formats of node_set_properties, such as [0, 3, 0] for a Vector3 or true for visible.

interpolation.description: How values blend between keys. Default: linear; linear_angle turns rotations the short way.

update.description: continuous blends every frame, discrete changes at each key. Default: discrete for values that cannot blend, such as bool and text, continuous otherwise.

path.description: The node whose methods are called, relative to the parent of the player, such as "Walker" or "." for the parent itself.

time.description: Seconds from the start of the animation.

method.description: The method to call, such as "_on_footstep"; it must already exist in the script of the node.

args.description: Arguments in order, in the formats of node_set_properties, such as ["left"]. Default: none.

path.description: An AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStreamPlayer2D or AudioStreamPlayer3D, relative to the parent of the player, such as "Walker/Footsteps".

time.description: Seconds from the start of the animation.

stream.description: The sound to play, as a res:// path such as "res://sounds/step.ogg".

start_offset.description: Seconds cut from the start of the sound. Default: 0.

end_offset.description: Seconds cut from the end of the sound. Default: 0.

tracks.description: One track per animated property, per node whose methods are called and per audio player, each with all its keys.

scene.description: The scene, as a res:// path; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: animation_delete
tools.description: Delete an animation of an AnimationPlayer as one Undo step.

player.description: Path of the AnimationPlayer relative to the scene root, such as "AnimationPlayer" or "Door/AnimationPlayer".

name.description: Name of the animation, such as "open"; "library/name" for an animation of another library than the default one.

scene.description: The scene, as a res:// path; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: animation_tree_get
tools.description: Read an AnimationTree: the AnimationPlayer it takes animations from, whether it is active, and for a state machine its states, the transitions between them with their conditions and expressions, and the condition parameters that scripts set.

tree.description: Path of the AnimationTree relative to the scene root, such as "AnimationTree" or "Player/AnimationTree".

scene.description: The scene, as a res:// path; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: animation_tree_set
tools.description: Set up an AnimationTree as a state machine, as one Undo step: states that each play an animation of the AnimationPlayer or blend several by a parameter, such as walking and running by speed, and transitions between them, such as {"from": "Start", "to": "idle"} and {"from": "idle", "to": "walk", "condition": "moving", "xfade": 0.2}. It replaces the tree root; states or transitions the editor cannot use are rejected with the reason and the rest are kept. Scripts switch states by setting conditions, such as $AnimationTree.set("parameters/conditions/moving", true), or with travel("walk") on parameters/playback. In the running game, set a condition with game_set_properties on the AnimationTree and wait for a state with game_wait and the condition get("parameters/playback").get_current_node() == "walk".

tree.description: Path of the AnimationTree relative to the scene root, such as "AnimationTree" or "Player/AnimationTree".

player.description: Path of the AnimationPlayer whose animations the states play, relative to the scene root. Default: the one the tree already uses.

name.description: Name of the state, such as "walk".

animation.description: The animation of the AnimationPlayer that the state plays, such as "walk". Give either animation or blend.

blend.description: Blend animations by a parameter instead of playing one: [{"animation": "walk", "at": 2}, {"animation": "run", "at": 6}] blends walking and running by speed (BlendSpace1D); points at [x, y] blend in two dimensions (BlendSpace2D), which needs three points that are not on one line. Scripts set the position with parameters/<state>/blend_position.

animation.description: An animation of the AnimationPlayer, such as "run".

at.description: Where the animation plays fully: a number, such as the speed 6, or [x, y] in a two-dimensional blend, such as [1, 0] for strafing right.

min.description: The lowest blend position, a number or [x, y] like the points. Default: the lowest point.

max.description: The highest blend position, a number or [x, y] like the points. Default: the highest point.

states.description: The states, each playing one animation of the AnimationPlayer or blending several, such as [{"name": "idle", "animation": "idle"}, {"name": "move", "blend": [{"animation": "walk", "at": 2}, {"animation": "run", "at": 6}]}].

transitions.description: Transitions between the states. The machine begins at Start, so give one from Start to the first state. Default: none.

from.description: The state the transition leaves; "Start" for the entry of the machine.

to.description: The state the transition enters; "End" for the exit of the machine.

condition.description: Take the transition when parameters/conditions/<condition> is true, such as "moving".

expression.description: Take the transition when this Godot expression is true, evaluated on the node in the tree's advance_expression_base_node, such as "velocity.length() > 0.1".

advance.description: auto takes the transition by itself, enabled only when travel() asks for it, disabled never. Default: auto from Start and with a condition or expression, enabled otherwise.

switch.description: When to switch: immediate (default), sync keeps the play position, at_end waits for the animation to end.

priority.description: Lower numbers win when several transitions could be taken. Default: 1.

scene.description: The scene, as a res:// path; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: autoload_add
tools.description: Register a script or scene as an autoload: Godot creates it when the game starts and keeps it as a global node that every script reaches by its name, such as GameState.score. Use it for game-wide state, settings and managers. Saves project.godot at once.

name.description: The global name of the autoload that scripts use, such as "GameState".

path.description: The script or scene to create when the game starts, as a res:// path, such as "res://autoload/game_state.gd". A script must extend Node.

tools.name: autoload_remove
tools.description: Remove an autoload from the project and save project.godot. Its script or scene file stays; scripts that use the autoload name fail until they are changed.

name.description: The global name of the autoload that scripts use, such as "GameState".

tools.name: node_set_groups
tools.description: Add a node to groups or take it out of them, as one Undo step; the groups are saved with the scene. Scripts find the nodes of a group with get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies"), and node_find finds them by group.

path.description: Path of the node relative to the scene root, such as "Player/Camera"; "." is the root itself.

add.description: Groups to add the node to, such as ["enemies", "damageable"].

remove.description: Groups to take the node out of.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: editor_select
tools.description: Select nodes in the scene tree of the editor, or a file in its FileSystem dock, to show the user what you are talking about; the inspector shows what is selected. Changes nothing in the project.

nodes.description: Paths of the nodes to select in the scene tree, such as ["Player", "Player/Camera"].

scene.description: The scene of the nodes, as a res:// path; the editor switches to it. Default: the scene open in the editor.

file.description: A file or folder to select in the FileSystem dock instead, such as "res://materials/ice.tres".

tools.name: editor_undo
tools.description: Take back the last actions in a scene's Undo history, as Ctrl+Z in the editor does, and name them. Every change these tools make is one action named "MCP: …"; by default only those are taken back, and it stops at an action of the user. Redo them with editor_redo.

count.description: How many actions to step through, newest first. Default: 1.

include_user_actions.description: Also step through actions that the user made in the editor. Default: false, so only the actions of these tools, named "MCP: …", are taken back or done again.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: editor_redo
tools.description: Do again the actions that editor_undo or the user took back in a scene, as Ctrl+Shift+Z in the editor does, and name them. By default only actions of these tools, named "MCP: …", are done again.

count.description: How many actions to step through, newest first. Default: 1.

include_user_actions.description: Also step through actions that the user made in the editor. Default: false, so only the actions of these tools, named "MCP: …", are taken back or done again.

scene.description: The scene to change, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project; it is opened in the editor if it is not open yet. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

tools.name: editor_get_state
tools.description: Show what the user is looking at in the Godot editor: the scene on screen and the main screen (3D, 2D or Script), the nodes selected in the Scene dock, the files selected in the FileSystem dock, the script open in the script editor with the line of its caret and the selected text, and the open scenes. Use it when the user says "this node", "the selected object", "this script" or "here".

tools.name: scene_close
tools.description: Close a scene in the editor: the one named, or the one open now. A scene with unsaved changes stays open unless unsaved says to save them first or to discard them.

scene.description: The scene to close, as a res:// path or "main" for the main scene of the project. Default: the scene currently open in the editor.

unsaved.description: What to do with unsaved changes: "save" saves them first, "discard" drops them. Without it, a scene with unsaved changes stays open.

tools.name: script_rename_symbol
tools.description: Rename a function, signal, variable, constant, enum or class_name across the project with the editor's language server, which renames every use it can trace in the scripts; then also the method names of signal connections, the keys of method tracks, saved values and animated paths in scenes and resources that use the script, which a rename in code alone leaves broken. It lists the places that still name the old symbol, such as strings in call() or has_method(), to check by hand. Save open files first; needs the editor.

path.description: The script that declares the symbol, as a res:// path, such as "res://enemy.gd".

symbol.description: The function, signal, variable, constant, enum or class_name to rename, such as "take_damage".

tools.name: script_find_references
tools.description: Find where a function, signal, variable, constant, enum or class_name is declared and used across the project, such as before changing the arguments of a function or removing it. Unlike a text search, it tells them apart from the uses of a symbol of the same name in another script, such as take_damage of Enemy from take_damage of Barrel. The editor's language server traces the uses in scripts, also through typed variables and class names; then come the signal connections, method track keys, saved values and animated properties of scenes and resources that use the script, which the language server does not see, and the lines that name the symbol where it could not be traced, such as calls on untyped variables or strings in call() and has_method(). Lines count from 1. Needs the editor.

path.description: The script that declares the symbol, as a res:// path, such as "res://enemy.gd".

symbol.description: The function, signal, variable, constant, enum or class_name to look for, such as "take_damage".

tools.name: script_validate
tools.description: Check GDScript files for errors and warnings without running the game, as the Godot editor does: syntax, types, unknown identifiers, unused variables; and compile .gdshader files with Godot's shader compiler, which reports the first error of each shader with its line, also inside included files. Call it after writing or changing .gd or .gdshader files, before game_run. Scripts are checked with the editor's language server, or godot --check-only when the editor is not connected; shaders in the editor, or in Godot without a window.

paths.description: Scripts, shaders or folders to check, as res:// paths or paths in the project, such as ["res://player/player.gd"], ["res://shaders/water.gdshader"] or ["res://player/"]. Folders are searched for .gd and .gdshader files; addons are skipped unless named.

tools.name: plugin_set_enabled
tools.description: Turn an editor plugin of res://addons on or off, as Project Settings → Plugins does: in the running editor, or in project.godot when no editor runs, so that the editor loads it when it starts. Plugins add tools to the editor, such as a test runner; their autoloads and custom node types come with them.

plugin.description: The plugin, by its folder in res://addons, such as "gut", or by its plugin.cfg, such as "res://addons/gut/plugin.cfg".

enabled.description: true (default) turns the plugin on, false turns it off.

tools.name: test_install_framework
tools.description: Install a test framework into the project and enable its plugin, so that test_run can run the project's tests: GUT 9.7.1 (default) or gdUnit4 6.2.2, each pinned to the commit of its release and fetched from GitHub with git. It downloads code, so the user confirms every call.

framework.description: gut (default) installs GUT, gdunit4 installs gdUnit4.

tools.name: test_run
tools.description: Run the project's GUT or gdUnit4 tests in a separate Godot process and report the result: how many passed, failed and were skipped, each failure with its file, line and message, and test scripts that failed to load. Tests load scenes and resources from disk, so save changes first with scene_save. Works without the editor.

paths.description: Test folders or scripts to run, as res:// paths, such as ["res://test/"] or ["res://test/test_player.gd"]. Default: res://test and res://tests, or the folders that .gutconfig.json names.

name.description: Run only the tests whose names contain this text, such as "dash". GUT only: gdUnit4 runs whole test suites.

framework.description: The test framework, needed only when the project has both GUT and gdUnit4 in addons/.

headless.description: Run without a window. Set false for tests that need rendering or real input events; a window opens while they run.

timeout_ms.description: Stop the run after this many milliseconds.

tools.name: export_preset_add
tools.description: Add an export preset for a platform to export_presets.cfg, with the default options of that platform, so that export_project can export the game; mode "pack" of export_project needs no export templates. The editor reads presets when it starts, so its Export dialog shows a preset added while it runs only after a restart.

platform.description: The platform to export to, as Project → Export names it.

name.description: The name of the preset, which export_project takes. Default: the platform name.

export_path.description: Where the export goes, inside the project folder, such as "build/linux/capsule-walk.x86_64". Default: build/<platform>/ with the game name and the extension of the platform.

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Export the game with an export preset of the project, as Project → Export does, in a separate Godot process: a release or debug build, or only the game data as a .pck. The result lists the written files with their sizes and the warnings of the export. It writes only into a folder of its own inside the project, such as build/, which gets a .gdignore file so the editor does not import the exported files. Scenes and scripts are read from disk, so save changes first with scene_save. Release and debug builds need the export templates of the platform; when they are missing, the result says how to get them. Works without the editor.

preset.description: The export preset, by its name in Project → Export, such as "macOS" or "Windows Desktop". Default: the only preset of the project.

mode.description: "release" or "debug" builds the game with the export templates of the platform; "pack" writes only the game data as a .pck or .zip file, which needs no export templates and runs with a Godot executable of the same version. Default: "release".

output.description: Where to write the export, with the file name, inside the project folder, such as "build/macos/game.zip"; the extension picks the format. Default: the export path of the preset, ending in .pck in mode "pack".

timeout_ms.description: Stop the export after this many milliseconds.

tools.name: docs_class
tools.description: Read the reference of the installed Godot version for a class: what it inherits, its properties, methods with their signatures, signals, enums and constants, each with a short summary; with member, the full description of one of them. Covers engine classes, built-in types such as Vector3, @GlobalScope functions such as lerp, and the class_name classes of the project. Use it before writing code with an API you are unsure of.

name.description: A class such as "CharacterBody3D", a built-in type such as "Vector3", a class_name of the project, or "@GlobalScope"; "Class.member" works too.

member.description: One property, method, signal, constant or enum of the class to show in full, such as "move_and_slide". Inherited members are found too.

tools.name: docs_search
tools.description: Search the reference of the installed Godot version and the project's own classes by words in class and member names and their summaries, such as "raycast", "tween" or "look at". Returns classes and members to read with docs_class.

query.description: Words to look for in class and member names and their summaries, such as "raycast", "tween" or "look at".

tools.name: game_run
tools.description: Run the game and return its first output: the main scene by default, the scene open in the editor, or a scene by path. Waits until the game is ready, then watches it for a second, or for duration_ms and stops it. Runs from the editor, which saves the open scenes and scripts first; without the editor, starts Godot as a separate process. Script errors do not pause the game unless break_on_error is set; they come with file, line and stack.

scene.description: What to run: "main" (the main scene of the project), "current" (the scene open in the editor), or a res://….tscn path. Default: "main".

duration_ms.description: Keep the game running this long after it is ready, then stop it. Without it, the game keeps running after the first second of output.

fixed_fps.description: Run with a fixed frame rate, such as 60: every frame advances the game by exactly 1/fps seconds, so runs repeat exactly. Game time then no longer follows the clock, and without a window the game runs as fast as it can, so count waits and holds in physics frames.
