debug_draw.description: Draw debug shapes in the game, as the Debug menu of the editor does: "collisions" for collision shapes, "navigation" for navigation meshes, "paths" for Path3D curves, "avoidance" for avoidance radii. Screenshots then show why a body falls through a floor or a path takes a detour.

arguments.description: Arguments for the game, which its scripts read with OS.get_cmdline_user_args(), such as ["--level=3"].

window_size.description: Size of the game window [width, height] in pixels, such as [1280, 720], to check the layout at another size.

locale.description: Run the game in this locale, such as "de" or "pt_BR", to check its translations.

break_on_error.description: Stop the game in the debugger at its first script error, as at a breakpoint, so that debug_state shows the stack and the variables there. Default: false, the game runs on. Needs the editor.

tools.name: game_stop
tools.description: Stop the running game.

tools.name: game_get_output
tools.description: Read what the game printed since the last call: messages, warnings and errors with file, line and stack, plus errors the editor reported, such as script parse errors. Pass levels: ["error"] for errors only, or from_start to read the current run again from its start.

levels.description: Only these levels, such as ["error"]. Default: all.

from_start.description: Read the current run from its start instead of only what came after the last call.

max_entries.description: The most entries to return; call again for the rest.

tools.name: game_get_tree
tools.description: Show the node tree of the running game, including nodes it created while running, such as spawned enemies or bullets: names, types, scripts, instanced scenes and groups. With controls: true, list the visible buttons, labels and other controls with their rectangles and states instead. Needs a game started with game_run, with or without the editor.

path.description: Show only this subtree: a path relative to the current scene, such as "Enemies", or "/root" for the whole tree with the autoloads. Default: the current scene.

max_depth.description: How many levels below the first node to show.

max_nodes.description: The most nodes to list; hidden children are counted.

controls.description: List the visible controls instead: buttons, labels, text fields, sliders and bars, with their rectangles in game-view pixels, their text and whether they are disabled, pressed or focused, so that a menu can be read and clicked without a screenshot.

tools.name: game_get_properties
tools.description: Read properties of a node in the running game, or of several nodes in the same frame, like the remote inspector: positions, velocities, health, and getters such as is_on_floor(). Use it to check what the game is doing after game_run or game_wait. Needs a game started with game_run, with or without the editor.

path.description: Path of the node in the running game: relative to the current scene, such as "Player"; "." for the scene root; or absolute, such as "/root/GameState" for an autoload.

paths.description: Read several nodes at once instead of path, such as ["Player", "Enemy"]. They are read in the same frame, so their values belong together, such as the distance between them.

names.description: Properties to read, such as ["position", "velocity"], or paths such as "position:y" or "mesh:size". Methods without arguments whose names start with is_, get_, has_ or can_ can be read too, such as "is_on_floor()". Default: every property whose value differs from its default.

include_defaults.description: Without names, also list properties at their default values. The list gets long.

tools.name: game_set_properties
tools.description: Change properties of a node in the running game to try something out, such as moving the player or raising its speed, including variables of its script without @export, such as a score; a setter of the variable runs. The change lasts until the game stops; scene files stay as they are. Every value is read back. Needs a game started with game_run, with or without the editor.

path.description: Path of the node in the running game: relative to the current scene, such as "Player"; "." for the scene root; or absolute, such as "/root/GameState" for an autoload.

properties.description: Property names mapped to values, such as {"position": [0, 1, 0], "mesh": {"new": "BoxMesh", "size": [2, 1, 2]}}. Formats: numbers, booleans and text as JSON; vectors as [x, y, z] or "Vector3(0, 1, 0)"; rotation is in radians, rotation_degrees takes degrees; colors as "#ff8800", "orange" or [r, g, b, a] with channels from 0 to 1; enums by option name ("Double-Sided") or number; flags as a list of names; physics, render and navigation layers as a list of layer numbers or of the names the project gives them (["world", "enemies", 5]); resources as a "res://…" path, or {"new": "Class", …properties} to create one; the items of a Theme as "Button/styles/normal" or "Label/font_sizes/font_size", the points of a curve as "point_count", "point_0/position" and the handles "point_0/in" and "point_0/out", the items of a MeshLibrary as "item/0/name" and "item/0/mesh"; a script as "res://….gd"; node references and node paths, such as node_a of a joint, as paths relative to the node ("../Player") or to the scene root ("Player"); Transform3D, Basis, AABB and Rect2 in Godot syntax ("Transform3D(…)"). Scripting properties such as global_position work too. A path changes one part only: "mesh:size" a property of the node's own mesh, "position:y" one coordinate. Every value is read back after it is set.

tools.name: game_wait
tools.description: Wait in the running game until a condition holds on a node, such as "is_on_floor()" on Player, until a node emits a signal, such as "died", or for a number of physics frames, frames or milliseconds. Pass exactly one of condition, signal, physics_frames, frames or ms. While game_pause holds the game, game_wait plays it until then and pauses it again on that frame, such as at the top of a jump with "velocity.y <= 0". Needs a game started with game_run, with or without the editor.

condition.description: Wait until this Godot expression is true on the node, such as "is_on_floor()" or "position.y < 0.1". It is checked after every physics frame.

signal.description: Instead of a condition, wait until the node emits this signal, such as "died" or "landed", and return its arguments.

node.description: The node the condition is evaluated on, or that emits the signal, such as "Player". Default: the current scene root.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the condition or the signal before giving up. Default: 10 seconds.

physics_frames.description: Instead of a condition, wait this many physics frames (60 per second by default).

frames.description: Instead of a condition, wait this many rendered frames.

ms.description: Instead of a condition, wait this many milliseconds.

tools.name: game_input
tools.description: Play input into the running game step by step: hold input actions, keys, gamepad buttons and sticks, move, click, drag and scroll the mouse, click a Control by its path, touch and drag fingers, type text, wait, and read nodes or take screenshots at exact moments, such as the height of a jump 10 physics frames after the press, which a later call would miss. A hold of N physics frames lasts exactly N frames of the game. While game_pause holds the game, the input plays it only for its holds and waits, then pauses it again. Also check the result with game_get_properties or a screenshot right after the last step (screenshot: true). Actions must exist in the project when the game starts. Needs a game started with game_run, with or without the editor.

action.description: An input action of the project, such as "jump".

strength.description: How strongly the action is pressed, from 0 to 1. Default: 1.

state.description: "tap" (default) presses, holds and releases; "down" only presses; "up" only releases.

physics_frames.description: How long to hold, in physics frames (60 per second by default). Default: 2.

ms.description: How long to hold, in milliseconds.

key.description: A key name, such as "W", "Space", "Escape" or "Ctrl+S".

meta.description: Hold Meta (Cmd on macOS) with the key.

state.description: "tap" (default) presses, holds and releases; "down" only presses; "up" only releases.

physics_frames.description: How long to hold, in physics frames (60 per second by default). Default: 2.

ms.description: How long to hold, in milliseconds.

joypad_button.description: A gamepad button: a, b, x, y, back, guide, start, left_stick, right_stick, left_shoulder, right_shoulder, dpad_up, dpad_down, dpad_left or dpad_right.

state.description: "tap" (default) presses, holds and releases; "down" only presses; "up" only releases.

physics_frames.description: How long to hold, in physics frames (60 per second by default). Default: 2.

ms.description: How long to hold, in milliseconds.

joypad_motion.description: A gamepad axis: left_x, left_y, right_x, right_y, trigger_left or trigger_right.

value.description: Where to hold the axis, from -1 to 1: left and up are negative, and a trigger goes from 0 to 1. Needed unless state is "up", which centers it again.

state.description: "tap" (default) presses, holds and releases; "down" only presses; "up" only releases.

physics_frames.description: How long to hold, in physics frames (60 per second by default). Default: 2.

ms.description: How long to hold, in milliseconds.

mouse_motion.description: Move the mouse by [dx, dy] pixels of the game view, such as for mouse look.

click.description: Click at [x, y] in pixels of the game view, as in game screenshots, or on the middle of a visible Control by its path, such as "Menu/Resume".

state.description: "tap" (default) clicks; "down" presses the button and keeps it held, so that mouse_motion steps drag; "up" releases it.

wheel.description: Turn the mouse wheel, such as to zoom a camera or scroll a list.

at.description: Where the mouse is, [x, y] in pixels of the game view. Default: where it already is.

clicks.description: How many notches to turn. Default: 1.

touch.description: Touch the screen at [x, y] in pixels of the game view.

finger.description: Which finger, from 0 to 9, for gestures with several fingers. Default: 0.

state.description: "tap" (default) presses, holds and releases; "down" only presses; "up" only releases.

physics_frames.description: How long to hold, in physics frames (60 per second by default). Default: 2.

ms.description: How long to hold, in milliseconds.

touch_drag.description: Drag a finger that is down by [dx, dy] pixels of the game view.

finger.description: Which finger, from 0 to 9, for gestures with several fingers. Default: 0.

text.description: Type this text, as into a focused LineEdit.

read.description: A node of the running game to read at this moment of the input, such as "Player", as in game_get_properties.

names.description: Properties and getters to read, such as ["position", "velocity", "is_on_floor()"]. The result lists them with the physics frames played since the input began.

screenshot.description: Take a screenshot at this moment; up to 6 screenshots of one input, the final one included, come back as one labelled image.

steps.description: Input to play in order, such as [{"action": "move_forward", "ms": 1000}, {"action": "jump"}, {"wait_physics_frames": 10}, {"read": "Player", "names": ["position"]}, {"mouse_motion": [120, 0]}, {"click": [640, 360]}, {"wait_ms": 300}].

release_at_end.description: Release every action and key that is still held after the last step. Default: true.

screenshot.description: Take a screenshot of the game window right after the last step, as game_screenshot does, so that it shows the moment the input ends.

watch_signals.description: Signals to watch while the input plays; the result lists every emission with its step, physics frame and arguments, such as to check that "landed" is emitted exactly once.

node.description: The node that emits the signal, such as "Player". Default: the current scene root.

tools.name: game_record_input
tools.description: Record what a person does in the running game, such as the walk and jump that make a bug happen, and get it back as steps of game_input: the input actions, keys, mouse, gamepad and touch input with the physics frames between them. Start it, let the person play, then stop it. Input that game_input itself plays is not recorded. Replayed from the same starting state with fixed_fps, the steps repeat the playthrough, so they can reproduce a bug or become a test. Needs a game started with game_run, with or without the editor.

state.description: "start" begins recording the input of the person who plays the running game; "stop" ends it and returns the steps.

tools.name: game_screenshot
tools.description: See the running game: a screenshot of its window with the UI, a strip of frames a given number of physics frames apart, or renders of its 3D world from other angles that leave the game camera alone. Returns the image and the path of its file. Pixel positions in a screenshot of the window are the positions that game_input clicks use. Needs a game started with game_run that has a window, with or without the editor.

views.description: Render the 3D scene from these angles instead of the game window, up to 6 in one labelled image: a preset "front" (from +Z), "back", "left" (from -X), "right", "top" or "iso", framed on the whole scene; {"preset": "front", "target": "Player"} to frame one node; or {"position": [0, 8, 12], "look_at": [0, 0, 0]} for a camera at a point. Each view also takes "fov", "label" and "render", such as {"preset": "iso", "render": "unshaded"}.

target.description: A node to frame instead of the whole scene, such as "Player".

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees. Default: 50.

label.description: Caption of the view in the image.

render.description: Draw this view as a debug view of the 3D viewport instead of with materials and light: "unshaded" shows colors without light, to tell a dark room from a black material; "lighting" shows only the light; "overdraw" shows where transparent surfaces pile up; "wireframe" shows the triangles (editor_screenshot only); "normals" shows the surface normals (Forward+ only).

position.description: Camera position [x, y, z] in world coordinates.

look_at.description: The point the camera looks at. Default: the center of target, or of the whole scene.

target.description: A node to frame instead of the whole scene, such as "Player".

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees. Default: 50.

label.description: Caption of the view in the image.

render.description: Draw this view as a debug view of the 3D viewport instead of with materials and light: "unshaded" shows colors without light, to tell a dark room from a black material; "lighting" shows only the light; "overdraw" shows where transparent surfaces pile up; "wireframe" shows the triangles (editor_screenshot only); "normals" shows the surface normals (Forward+ only).

frames.description: Instead of one moment, take this many screenshots of the game window, every_physics_frames apart, as one labelled image, to see motion such as a jump, an animation or a camera move. While game_pause holds the game, it plays exactly those frames and pauses again.

every_physics_frames.description: Physics frames between the screenshots of frames. Default: 5.

max_size.description: The longest side of the image in pixels. Default: 1280.

format.description: png (default), or jpeg for a smaller file.

compare_to.description: Compare the new picture with an earlier one, by the path that an earlier screenshot gave (the last 100 are kept) or as an image of the project, such as "res://screenshots/level.png": the result says how much changed and where, and outlines the changes in the picture. Take both with the same views and size. Time, particles and temporal anti-aliasing make two runs differ; run the game with fixed_fps and take both at the same physics frame to compare runs.

tolerance.description: With compare_to, how much a color channel may change, from 0 to 1, before its pixel counts as changed. Default: 0.1.

tools.name: game_pause
tools.description: Pause the running game so that nothing moves, or resume it with paused: false. While it is paused, game_get_properties, game_screenshot and node_get_bounds read a frozen moment; game_step advances it by exact physics frames, and game_input and game_wait play it only for their holds and waits, then pause it again. Input sent while it is paused reaches the game in the next frame it plays. Nodes that the game sets to always process keep running. Needs a game started with game_run, with or without the editor.

tools.name: game_step
tools.description: Advance the paused game by exactly the given number of physics frames and keep it paused, to check what happens frame by frame, such as the height of a jump after 10 frames. Input sent while the game is paused reaches it in the first of these frames. A running game is paused after the frames. Needs a game started with game_run, with or without the editor.

physics_frames.description: How many physics frames to advance the game by (60 per second by default).

tools.name: game_performance
tools.description: Measure how the running game performs over a number of frames: frame time and FPS, time spent in process and physics code, draw calls and primitives, memory, counts of objects and nodes with orphan nodes (a sign of leaks), the load of 3D physics, the custom monitors the game adds with Performance.add_custom_monitor(), and in a game started from the editor the script functions that took the most time, with their files and lines. Needs a game started with game_run, with or without the editor.

tools.name: debug_breakpoints
tools.description: Add or remove breakpoints in GDScript files, or list them. The game stops at a breakpoint when its code reaches that line while it runs from the editor (game_run), and debug_state then shows the stack and the variables there. They are the editor's own breakpoints, so the user sees them in the script editor; clear removes all of them, also those the user set. A breakpoint on an empty line or a comment never stops the game.

add.description: Breakpoints to add, each "res://path.gd:line" with the line counted from 1, such as ["res://player/player.gd:42"].

remove.description: Breakpoints to remove, written the same way.

clear.description: Remove every breakpoint of the project first, also those the user set in the script editor.

tools.name: debug_state
tools.description: Show where the game stopped in the debugger and why — a breakpoint, a step or an error — with the stack of function calls, the code around the line, and the local variables and members of a stack frame; with expression, also the value of a GDScript expression in that frame. With wait_ms it first waits for the game to stop, such as after game_input made the player do what reaches the breakpoint. While the game is stopped, game_get_properties still reads nodes, but game_wait, game_input and screenshots need debug_continue first.

wait_ms.description: When the game is not stopped, wait this long for it to stop at a breakpoint, such as after game_input made the player jump. Default: 0, answer at once.

frame.description: The stack frame whose code and variables to show: 0 is the line where the game stopped, 1 the function that called it, and so on.

expression.description: A GDScript expression to evaluate in that frame, with its locals and members, such as "health - amount" or "get_node('Camera').position".

tools.name: debug_continue
tools.description: Resume the game stopped in the debugger, until the next breakpoint, or by one line of code at a time. After a step the result shows the new line and its variables.

action.description: "continue" runs the game until the next breakpoint; "step_over" runs the current line and stops at the next one; "step_into" also stops inside the functions that the line calls; "step_out" runs to the end of the current function and stops in the one that called it. Default: "continue".

instructions:
Tools for building a Godot 4 game (3D, GDScript) through the running Godot editor.
- Start with godot_status. If the editor is not connected, start it with editor_launch, or ask the user to open the project in Godot with the "Godot MCP Tool" plugin enabled; without it, the tools that read the project and its scenes, game_run and the other game_ tools, script_validate, test_run, export_project and the docs tools still work.
- Call project_info once per session: main scene, autoloads, global classes, and the indentation of .gd files. Never mix tabs and spaces.
- Write GDScript for Godot 4 only: @export, @onready, await, signal.connect(callable), CharacterBody3D, Node3D. When unsure about an engine API, read it with docs_class (or find it with docs_search) before writing code: it is the reference of the installed Godot build.
- While the editor is connected, change scenes and resources only with the scene_, node_ and resource_ tools, never by editing .tscn or .tres files as text. Edit .gd files with your own file tools; after creating or changing scripts that scenes use, call editor_rescan.
- Move or rename project files with filesystem_move rather than shell commands: it updates the scenes, resources and project settings that use them. Check what uses a file with resource_find_usages.
- Before changing a function's arguments or removing it, find its uses with script_find_references, not Grep: it tells apart same-named functions of other classes.
- Learn node paths with scene_get_tree or node_find before changing a scene. rotation is in radians; use rotation_degrees for degrees.
- Build or rework a scene with scene_batch_edit: many node and signal changes in one call and one Undo step, and nothing changes if one of them fails. Connect signals with signal_connect once the method exists in the script.
- Changes stay unsaved until scene_save, as in the editor. Save when a logical change is complete; game_run saves first, like the editor does.
- After writing or changing .gd files, check them with script_validate before running. Then check the result with game_run and read errors with game_get_output. Run the GUT or gdUnit4 tests of the project with test_run.
- To check how the running game behaves, play input with game_input (actions come from input_map_set), wait for a state with game_wait and read nodes with game_get_properties; getters such as is_on_floor() work there. The game keeps running between tool calls, which come seconds apart, so a short moment such as a jump in the air is over before a later call can read it: read it inside game_input with a read step, or pause the game with game_pause first, after which game_input, game_wait and game_step play it by exact physics frames and pause it again. Calls sent in one message may run one after another, so a game_wait sent with a game_input does not watch it.
- Check 3D placement and scale with numbers first (node_get_bounds), then look: game_screenshot shows the game window or views of its 3D world, editor_screenshot renders the open scene. One picture of a 3D scene can mislead, so use views from several angles, such as ["front", "top", "iso"].
- Imported models often arrive in centimeters: read their size with asset_import_settings_get and fix it with nodes/root_scale in asset_import_settings_set rather than by scaling nodes.
- To find out why game code misbehaves, stop it on a line with debug_breakpoints and game_run, then read the stack and the variables with debug_state and step with debug_continue; remove the breakpoints when done.
- When a result reports new errors (⚠), read them with game_get_output before you continue.
